title: ‘I Will Always Love You’: Why the world is mourning Dolly Parton
description:
Dolly Parton was a country music star like no other. Following her death from cancer on Tuesday, everyone from President Donald Trump to Beyoncé has expressed condolences online. But the public mourning isn’t just about Dolly’s catalogue of hits like “I Will Always Love You,” “Jolene” and “9 to 5,” or her nearly 50 studio albums like “Backwoods Barbie.”

William Lee Adams, a BBC culture reporter, explains why Dolly’s legacy has only grown with time. We discuss her uplifting personality, endlessly quotable quotes, and philanthropic endeavours — from donating a million dollars to help fund the Moderna Covid-19 vaccine to the Imagination Library, her charity that has gifted children more than 200 million free books.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討鄉村音樂巨星桃莉·芭頓 Dolly Parton 在 80 歲因癌症逝世後，全球各界的追思與她深遠的文化遺產。BBC 文化記者威廉·李·亞當斯 William Lee Adams 在節目中分享芭頓傳奇的職涯，包含創作 3,000 首歌曲、售出 1 億張唱片與榮獲 10 座葛萊美獎。除了經典歌曲 Jolene 與 I Will Always Love You 外，芭頓更以自嘲幽默與樂觀性格跨越政治與社會分歧。節目也深入介紹她的慈善事業，包括創立「想像力圖書館」 Imagination Library 捐贈超過 2 億冊童書、發放獎金將高中輟學率從 35% 降至 6% 、資助主題樂園員工大專學費，以及捐款 100 萬美元協助莫德納 Moderna 的 COVID-19 疫苗研發。芭頓以無條件的愛與對 LGBTQ+ 社群的支持，成為世人心中傳播善意與團結的文化象徵。
summaryEn: In this episode of BBC's What in the World, presenter Hannah Gelbart and BBC culture reporter William Lee Adams discuss the massive global legacy of country music star Dolly Parton following her death from cancer at age 80. Beyond her phenomenal musical achievements—writing 3,000 songs, selling 100 million records, and winning 10 Grammy Awards with hits like "Jolene" and "I Will Always Love You"—the episode explores why she was so uniquely beloved across political, social, and demographic divides. They highlight her humble Appalachian origin story, her quick-witted self-deprecating humor, and her extensive philanthropy, which included gifting over 200 million free books through the Imagination Library, drastically reducing high school dropout rates in her hometown, paying college tuition for her theme park staff, and donating $1 million to fund the Moderna COVID-19 vaccine. Ultimately, Parton is celebrated as a rare unifying figure who championed kindness, acceptance, and unconditional love.
